transcript.text: microwve plate wont go round anymore, food hot on one side cold on other. still heats tho

If it still heats but the plate no longer turns, the usual causes are:

• Plate/roller ring not seated properly
• Food debris or a broken roller ring
• The small plastic drive coupler in the centre is worn/cracked
• Failed turntable motor

Try this first, with the microwave unplugged:

1. Remove the glass plate and roller ring.
2. Clean underneath and make sure nothing is jammed.
3. Check the little centre spindle/coupler is present, not cracked, and sits firmly.
4. Put the roller ring and plate back so the plate properly engages with the centre drive.
5. Test it with a cup of water for 30–60 seconds.

Do not open the microwave casing—microwaves contain high-voltage parts that can remain dangerous even unplugged.

You can generally use it temporarily if it otherwise works, but pause and manually turn/stir the food halfway through. Be especially careful with meat, leftovers, and baby food: uneven heating can leave cold spots, so let food stand briefly and check it is hot all the way through.

If the plate still does not move after cleaning/reseating, it likely needs a turntable motor or coupler replacement. Those parts are often inexpensive, but whether repair is worthwhile depends on the microwave’s age and model.

ok did that. roller ring is fine, wheels turn and nothing stuck under it. the little 3 pronged plastic bit in the middle has a crack and the hole looks rounded. it wobbles and doesnt really turn when i run it with a cup of water

That sounds like the turntable drive coupler has failed. The crack and rounded-out centre hole mean it is no longer gripping the motor shaft properly, so the motor may be turning underneath but the coupler slips instead of driving the plate.

What to do:

1. Unplug the microwave.
2. Remove the glass tray and roller ring.
3. The 3-pronged piece usually pulls straight up off the metal motor shaft. It may need a gentle wiggle, but don’t force or pry aggressively.
4. Find the microwave’s model number (usually on a sticker inside the door frame, rear, or side) and search for:
   “[model number] turntable coupler” or “drive coupler.”
5. Fit the replacement by pressing it straight down onto the shaft, then reinstall the roller ring and plate.

Avoid trying to glue it: heat, grease, and the turning force usually make glue fail, and you do not want loose adhesive near food.

A new coupler is commonly cheap. If you replace it and the new one still does not rotate, then the turntable motor or its shaft may be the issue—but based on the visible crack/wobble, the coupler is the most likely fix.
